Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-08 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-20261208-tdb-8347.mp3
Shared links: deck: https://tinyurl.com/tidalwave-optimize, console shortlink: https://rw.console/s/abc123, cost sheet: https://redwood.app/sims/tidalwave-2026

Summary (auto): walkthrough of Optimize suggestions for batching and prefix/KV prefetch. Pilot agreed.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Sofia Park: Hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. I'm Sofia, I'll run the high level and Marcus from SE will jump in with the cost sim and demo.
[00:12] Ravi Kapoor: Hi thanks, yep Ravi here. Maya and Jordan on my side. We're mainly focused on lowering token spend for our low-latency chat product.
[00:20] Marcus Li: Quick agenda, we'll show the Optimize console, load a sample job, run the prefetch sim with the KV cache profile, then show batch sizing scenarios with throughput numbers and cost delta.
[00:32] Maya Santos: Cool, our big constraints: 95th pct latency under 350ms, can't accept higher tail latencies; and all PII must not leave our VPC — we may need private deploy or at least strict network rules.
[00:48] Sofia Park: Got it. We'll highlight dedicated and private options and how prefetch interacts with VPC. Marcus, show the console.
[00:55] Marcus Li: Sure. Opening the console, Optimize > Prefetch tab — note sometimes the console label transcribed as 'Optima' in older logs. Here we upload the traffic trace, select model family (we used vicuna-13b-quant in the sim), and pick a prefix TTL.
[01:10] Marcus Li: (typing) The cost-sim shows baseline tokens at 1.9M tokens/day, with naive single-token streaming. If we apply prefix/KV prefetch for sessionized flows we see 28% token reduction by reusing cached KV states.
[01:28] Jordan Lee: Quick q, is the KV cache persisted on node-local memory or in an external cache? We need to know the network egress pattern.
[01:36] Marcus Li: Good point. In hosted we keep KV in process on the serving host; in Dedicated/Private we can pin an edge cache — in private/onprem you control whether to use an in-cluster memcached/redis or Redwood's local shm cache. That impacts egress.
[01:50] Maya Santos: So for our VPC, if we self-manage, we avoid egress. That would satisfy legal.
[01:56] Sofia Park: Exactly. Also discussed SOC2 and audit logs — we have an SOC2 package + KMS integration details in the security deck we will share.
[02:06] Marcus Li: Back to economics, here's the interesting tradeoff: larger batch sizes improve GPU utilization and lower per-token cost but increase scheduling latency. For our 350ms 95th, the sim suggests an optimal batch target around 16 concurrent requests given your median prompt length.
[02:26] Ravi Kapoor: 16 seems high; our peak concurrency is spiky — could we use adaptive batching?
[02:32] Marcus Li: Yes, Redwood runtime supports continuous batching with a latency budget. We can set a max latency target per route; it will flush early if latency budget would be exceeded. So in spikes it will favor lower latency, in steady state it will aggregate.
[02:45] Maya Santos: How does prefetch interact with batching? Does prefetching increase batch hit rates or reduce them?
[02:52] Marcus Li: Prefetch increases token efficiency by priming KV cache — if you prefetch common prefixes for sessionized flows you'll get higher KV hit rates so subsequent requests render fewer decoder tokens. That actually reduces batch payload size per request, which can lower jitter. But note prefetching itself consumes tokens — the sim models that.
[03:10] Sofia Park: I'll call out the sim numbers — baseline cost $3.4k/mo at current traffic; with prefix prefetch + medium batching we estimated $2.3k/mo, roughly a 32% saving. If you go heavy on prefetch and slightly higher batch targets, we saw up to 46% but latency tail increases.
[03:32] Ravi Kapoor: Those are promising. Can you show the sim assumptions?
[03:36] Marcus Li: Yep opening the spreadsheet: assumptions tab lists tokenization (BPE), model throughput (TPU equiv), quantization profile (8-bit q4), average prompt length 110 tokens, average response 48 tokens. Also shows failure cases where prefetch mispredicts and increases tokens.
[03:58] Maya Santos: On the quantization note, we run a custom finetune of an Llama fork. Any gotchas with kernel selection?
[04:06] Marcus Li: We do model profiling; if it's an uncommon arch we run a quick micro-benchmark. Sometimes kernel fallback causes slightly higher latency; we can flag that and recommend a specific kernel/quantization profile.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: About the pilot — we'd prefer a non-prod pilot behind our VPC. Can Redwood run a Dedicated pool inside our cloud account or do we need private cluster?
[04:28] Sofia Park: For pilots we typically do a Dedicated deployment with managed peering into your VPC; for stricter compliance we do Private with customer-controlled control-plane. We'll provide both options and a checklist.
[04:40] Marcus Li: I'll note network egress items — Jordan, we'll send the firewall list.
[04:45] Maya Santos: How long until we can get meaningful numbers? Week-ish?
[04:48] Marcus Li: If you can share 48-72h representative traces within a day, we can run a 48h sim and return a per-scenario cost delta in ~3 business days.
[04:58] Ravi Kapoor: Sounds good. A couple more technicals — how do you measure token savings from KV reuse? Do you rely on decoded-token counts or internal KV hit counters?
[05:06] Marcus Li: Both. We instrument the runtime with token counters and KV hit/miss metrics. Optimize ties those to cost models so you can attribute savings per-route and per-prompt template.
[05:16] Maya Santos: Any limits on prefix length for prefetch? We have prompts with long contexts.
[05:21] Marcus Li: The KV cache is keyed by prefix hash and we recommend prefetching up to 256 tokens of prefix in most cases. Beyond that you hit diminishing returns and larger memory pressure. We'll show examples in the pilot.
[05:31] Sofia Park: Quick interjection — competitor question: Ravi, did you evaluate other vendors?
[05:36] Ravi Kapoor: We looked at Anthropic's managed endpoints and a bunch of in-house options. Anthropic was ok but the cost profile didn't meet our throughput requirements.
[05:44] Marcus Li: Right — one differentiation is our Optimize tooling ties the runtime metrics to cost sims and rollouts, making it easier to A/B.
[05:51] (sound of papers)
[05:58] Marcus Li: Now I'll demo a live scenario. Import trace, select route filters for 'support-chat', pick prefetch TTL 30m, set batch latency budget 120ms, run sim.
[06:10] Marcus Li: (clicks) Here's the scenario results: tokens saved, estimated cost delta, expected 95th latency impact. Note the UI shows a confidence bar — this comes from historical variance.
[06:22] Maya Santos: That confidence bar — what underlies it? Sample size?
[06:25] Marcus Li: Yes, it's bootstrap sampling from your trace and runtime variance. Small traces give wider bars.
[06:31] Sofia Park: Also we attach an annotation with the assumptions for each sim so you can drill into prompt templates that drive savings.
[06:39] Ravi Kapoor: For SLA / rollouts, can we do canary that falls back if latency increases?
[06:44] Marcus Li: Absolutely — rollouts support traffic shaping: start at 10% with canary routing and automatic fallback to baseline model or lower batching if latency exceeds threshold.
[06:55] Jordan Lee: One last infra Q: when prefetch triggers, is the prefetch generated synchronously blocking user requests?
[07:02] Marcus Li: Prefetch can be async — we support background prefetch warmers that run ahead of traffic. But you can also do synchronous on-demand prefetch; tradeoffs exist. Async warmers cost tokens but keep tail latency low.
[07:15] Maya Santos: I worry about token costs for warmers during low-usage periods. Do you have heuristics?
[07:20] Marcus Li: Yes, Optimize has heuristics keyed to session heatmaps. E.g., only warm prefixes with >X hits in last Y hours. We'll tune those thresholds in the pilot.
[07:32] Sofia Park: Ok wrapping this into next steps — Marcus, you'll prepare the pilot spec and cost sheet. I'll share SOC2 and KMS docs. Maya and Jordan, you'll share sample traces and VPC egress list.
[07:45] Ravi Kapoor: Agreed. Also want a short doc on failure cases where prefetch harms cost.
[07:52] Marcus Li: We'll include that in the deliverables.
[07:55] (pause)
[08:00] [Timestamp jumps — summary notes inserted by the recorder]
[25:00] Marcus Li: (mid-call) Running a mid-sim where we push concurrency to simulate Black Friday - here batching wins big but tail suffers unless we lower latency budget. Example: batch 24 -> throughput up 3.1x but 95th rises ~120ms.
[30:14] Maya Santos: If we must keep 95th under 350ms, what's the maximum batch you recommend?
[30:22] Marcus Li: For your median profile it's around 18; above that we recommend aggressive prefetching + async warmers to offset latency.
[36:10] Sofia Park: Security note — we'll include an appendix on audit log retention and KMS integration steps for private.
[42:05] Jordan Lee: Pilot timeline accepted. We prefer pilot in our cloud account with Redwood Dedicated peered.
[45:30] Marcus Li: I'll prepare the Dedicated-run checklist and share infra playbook.
[50:01] Sofia Park: Recap: Sofia shares cost sheet and security docs; Marcus shares pilot spec and infra checklist; customer provides traces and firewall rules. We'll regroup after initial 48h sim.
[50:18] Ravi Kapoor: Yep thanks everyone. Good session.
[50:25] Maya Santos: Thanks.
[50:28] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
[50:32] Sofia Park: Thanks all — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the links.

End of recording.
